complexity.notes: Evaluate both expressions on every row; exact but exponential in the number of variables.

complexity.name: Quine-McCluskey prime-implicant generation
complexity.notes: Each cube fixes every position to 0, 1 or dash; a function can have up to about 3ⁿ/n prime implicants.

complexity.name: Minimum PI cover (Petrick's method)
complexity.notes: EPI extraction and row/column dominance shrink the chart in polynomial time; the residual cyclic core needs search.

problemTypes.title: Minimal SOP or POS of a 4-variable function with don't-cares
recipe: Plot the 1s and the don't-cares on a Gray-coded map; mark which cells wrap.
Circle every 1 that has only one possible largest group first: those groups are the EPIs.
Cover the remaining 1s with the fewest, largest groups, using don't-cares only where they enlarge a group.
Check each option by expanding it to minterms: it must cover every 1 and no 0.
problemTypes.trap: Two equally minimal covers often exist; an option is wrong only if it misses a 1, covers a 0, or uses more terms or literals.

problemTypes.title: Count prime and essential prime implicants
recipe: Plot the map and, for each 1-cell, find every maximal group containing it.
Collect the distinct maximal groups: that is the PI count, including PIs that no minimal cover uses.
A PI is essential when some true minterm (not a don't-care) lies in no other PI.
problemTypes.trap: Students count only the PIs of their chosen cover and miss the redundant ones, such as BC' in Σm(0, 1, 4, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15).

problemTypes.title: Simplify an expression with identities
recipe: Merge adjacent terms (XY + XY' = X) and absorb (X + XY = X).
Remove redundant literals (X + X'Y = X + Y) and consensus terms whose parents are both present.
When unsure, convert the expression and each option to minterm lists and compare.
problemTypes.trap: Removing a term as consensus when one parent is missing, as in reducing AB + AC + A'BC to AB + AC.

problemTypes.title: Count Boolean functions with a property
recipe: Ask what is free: one output per row (2^(2ⁿ)), per complementary row pair (self-dual), or per weight class (symmetric).
Fixed rows reduce the exponent: k fixed rows give 2^(2ⁿ − k).
Counting constraints on the number of 1s become binomial coefficients, as in C(8, 4) = 70 neutral 3-variable functions.

problemTypes.title: Minimum NAND or NOR gates for a function
recipe: Minimize the function first (SOP for NAND, POS for NOR).
Two-level form: one gate per multi-literal term plus one output gate; add an inverter per complemented input not available.
For XOR, XNOR and other small functions, recall the known minima (XOR 4 NANDs, XNOR 5) instead of the two-level count.
problemTypes.trap: The two-level count is not always minimal; XOR in two-level NAND form needs 5 gates with inverters, but 4 suffice with a shared NAND.

problemTypes.title: Is a gate set functionally complete?
recipe: Try to build NOT: if every operation outputs 0 on all-0 inputs (or 1 on all-1 inputs), NOT is impossible.
Check monotone (AND, OR), linear (XOR, XNOR) and self-dual classes; a set trapped in one class is incomplete.
If NOT plus AND or OR can be built, the set is complete.
problemTypes.trap: {XOR, AND} looks complete because A ⊕ 1 = A', but the constant 1 is not in the set.

problemTypes.title: Quine-McCluskey table: prime and essential implicants
recipe: Group minterms by number of 1s and merge neighbouring groups that differ in one bit.
Repeat on merged cubes with matching dash positions; unticked cubes are the PIs.
Build the PI chart on true minterms only and take the sole covers as EPIs, then finish with Petrick's method.
problemTypes.trap: Merging cubes whose dashes sit in different positions, or putting don't-cares in the chart's columns.

questions.stem: Simplify F = ABC + AB'C + ABC' + A'BC.
questions.explanation: The terms are minterms 7, 5, 6 and 3, the rows with at least two 1s. ABC + AB'C = AC, ABC + ABC' = AB and ABC + A'BC = BC (ABC may be reused). So F = AB + BC + CA, the majority function. AB + AC misses m3 = A'BC, which only BC covers, so BC is not a removable consensus term here.

Multiply out: AA' + AC + A'B + BC = AC + A'B + BC. BC is the consensus of AC and A'B, so it drops: AC + A'B. Check row A = 1, B = 1, C = 0: the original is 1·0 = 0, AC + A'B = 0, but AB + A'C = 1 and AC + A'B + AB = 1, so those are wrong.

questions.stem: The complement of (X + Y)(Y + Z) is:
questions.explanation: De Morgan on the product: (X + Y)' + (Y + Z)' = X'Y' + Y'Z' = Y'(X' + Z'). Option (X' + Y')(Y' + Z') complements the literals but keeps the operators. X'Y'Z' misses the row X = 1, Y = 0, Z = 0 where the original is 1·0 = 0. Y' + X'Z' is 1 at X = 0, Y = 1, Z = 0, where the original is 1.

questions.stem: For f = A + BC' + 0, which is the dual of f?
questions.explanation: The dual swaps + with · and 0 with 1 and keeps every literal: A + BC' + 0 becomes A · (B + C') · 1 = A(B + C'). A'(B' + C) is the complement of f (dual plus complemented literals). The other two options keep the operators and are neither.

questions.stem: Which is a minimal sum-of-products for F(A, B, C, D) = Σm(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)?
questions.explanation: The PIs are A'BD' (4, 6), AB'D' (8, 10), A'CD' (2, 6) and B'CD' (2, 10). Minterm 4 lies only in A'BD' and 8 only in AB'D', so both are essential; m2 is left and needs A'CD' or B'CD'. So B'CD' + A'BD' + AB'D' is minimal (9 literals). BD' covers m12 and m14, which are 0. A'B'CD' covers m2 but is not prime. BD' + B'D' = D' covers every even minterm, including the 0s 0, 12 and 14.

questions.stem: The minimal SOP of F(A, B, C) = Σm(1, 3, 7) + d(0, 2, 5) is:
questions.explanation: The column C = 1 holds m1, m3, m7 and the don't-care m5: one 4-cell group, F = C. A' + BC covers every 1 but costs 3 literals instead of 1. A'C + BC is valid but larger. A' + C also works but has an extra term; the single literal C is the unique minimum.

questions.stem: The minimal product-of-sums of F(A, B, C) = Σm(0, 2, 5, 7) is:
questions.explanation: The 0s are at 1 (001), 3 (011), 4 (100) and 6 (110). {1, 3} has A = 0, C = 1, giving sum term A + C'. {4, 6} has A = 1, C = 0, giving A' + C. F = (A + C')(A' + C), which is A ⊙ C. The second option is A ⊕ C, the complement. The last is the product of maxterms M1 and M4 only, so it would wrongly output 1 at rows 3 and 6.

questions.stem: Using a 5-variable K-map with A as the most significant bit, minimize F(A, B, C, D, E) = Σm(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 16, 18, 21, 23, 24, 26).
questions.explanation: In binary, 0, 2, 8, 10, 16, 18, 24, 26 all have C = 0 and E = 0 with A, B, D free: an 8-cell group across both halves, C'E'. The rest, 5, 7, 21, 23, are 00101, 00111, 10101, 10111: B = 0, C = 1, E = 1 with A and D free, B'CE. Splitting B'CE by A wastes a term, since cells at the same position in the A = 0 and A = 1 halves are adjacent. CE also covers 13 and 15, which are 0.

questions.stem: For F(A, B, C, D) = Σm(1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 15), which of the following are essential prime implicants?
questions.explanation: The tabular method gives six PIs: -001 = B'C'D, 01-0 = A'BD', 011- = A'BC, -111 = BCD, 1-11 = ACD and 10-- = AB'. Minterm 1 lies only in B'C'D, 4 only in A'BD' and 8 only in AB', so these three are essential. BCD is prime and appears in the minimal cover B'C'D + A'BD' + AB' + BCD, but it is not essential: 7 is also in A'BC and 15 in ACD.

questions.stem: How many prime implicants does F(A, B, C, D) = Σm(0, 1, 4, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15) have?
questions.explanation: Maximal groups: A'C' = {0, 1, 4, 5}, AB = {12, 13, 14, 15}, and BC' = {4, 5, 12, 13}, which cannot be enlarged because 0, 1, 8 and 9 are not all 1. So there are 3 PIs. A'C' (only cover of m0) and AB (only cover of m14) are essential; BC' is redundant, and F = A'C' + AB.

questions.stem: How many prime implicants does F(A, B, C) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7) have?
questions.explanation: Each 1-cell has two neighbouring 1s and no 4-cell group exists, so the PIs are the six pairs A'B' (0, 1), A'C' (0, 2), B'C (1, 5), BC' (2, 6), AC (5, 7) and AB (6, 7). Every minterm lies in exactly two of them, so none is essential; the two minimal covers A'B' + BC' + AC and A'C' + B'C + AB each use 3.

questions.stem: How many Boolean functions of 3 variables satisfy f(0, 0, 0) = 1?
questions.explanation: There are 2³ = 8 rows. Fixing one row's output leaves 7 rows free, each 0 or 1, so 2⁷ = 128 functions, half of the 256.

questions.stem: A Boolean function is called neutral if its truth table has as many 1s as 0s. How many neutral functions of 3 variables exist?
questions.explanation: The truth table has 8 rows; choose which 4 output 1: C(8, 4) = 8·7·6·5 / 4! = 70. The 16 self-dual functions are among them, since each is 1 on exactly half the rows.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of 2-input NAND gates needed to realize A ⊕ B, with only A and B available as inputs?
questions.explanation: Let T = NAND(A, B) = (AB)'. Then NAND(A, T) = (AT)' = (AB')' and NAND(B, T) = (A'B)', and NAND of these two is AB' + A'B = A ⊕ B: 4 gates. An exhaustive search over all 2-input NAND circuits finds none with 3 gates.

questions.stem: Which of these gate sets are functionally complete, with no constants available?
questions.explanation: NAND gives NOT as NAND(A, A) and then AND and OR, so it is complete. {OR, NOT} gives AND as (A' + B')'. {AND, OR} is monotone and cannot produce NOT. {XOR, AND} outputs 0 whenever all inputs are 0, so it cannot produce NOT without the constant 1; it reaches only the 128 of 256 three-variable functions with f(000) = 0.

questions.stem: Which of the following functions of A, B, C are self-dual?
questions.explanation: Self-dual means complementing all inputs complements the output. Majority: A'B' + B'C' + C'A' is 1 exactly when at most one input is 1, the complement of majority, so it is self-dual. XOR: A' ⊕ B' ⊕ C' = (A ⊕ B ⊕ C)', self-dual. AB + C is 1 on five rows, not four, so it cannot be. AB + A'C at 001 gives 1 and at 110 also gives 1, so it fails.

pitfalls.text: De Morgan changes two things: the operator flips and every literal is complemented. Doing only one gives (X' + Y')(Y' + Z') for the complement of (X + Y)(Y + Z).
A consensus term is redundant only while both parent terms remain. In AB + AC + BC with no A' term, BC is not a consensus and cannot be dropped.
K-map groups must be rectangles of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 cells; three 1s in a row or an L-shape is never one term. Remember the edges wrap.
Counting PIs means all maximal groups, including ones no minimal cover uses; counting EPIs means only those that solely cover a true minterm.
Don't-cares are optional: use one only when it enlarges a group, and never let a don't-care cell decide that a PI is essential.
In POS, a 0-group with A = 0 contributes the literal A, not A'. Read sum terms with the opposite polarity to product terms.
The dual keeps literals and swaps operators and constants; the complement also complements literals. Confusing them is the most common error on self-dual questions.
AND, OR and XOR are each incomplete, and so are {XOR, AND} and {AND, OR}; only NAND or NOR alone is universal among two-input gates.

errata.claim: The prime implicants of Σm(0, 1, 4, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15) are only A'C' and AB.
errata.correction: BC' = {4, 5, 12, 13} is also a prime implicant, so there are 3 PIs. It is not essential, and the minimal SOP stays A'C' + AB.

errata.claim: After the essential PIs, the remaining minterms are covered by choosing PIs greedily.
errata.correction: Greedy selection can miss the minimum cover. An exact minimum needs Petrick's method or an exhaustive search of the reduced PI chart.

errata.claim: F = Σm(1, 3, 7) + d(0, 2, 5) minimizes to A' + BC.
errata.correction: The column C = 1 (m1, m3, m7 with don't-care m5) forms one 4-cell group, so the minimal SOP is F = C.
Without the constant 1, XOR and AND both output 0 on all-0 inputs, so NOT cannot be built and the set is incomplete. The Reed-Muller basis is {XOR, AND, 1}.

errata.claim: Example 5: for F = ΠM(0, 2, 4, 6), grouping the 0s gives F' = C and F = C'.
errata.correction: The 0s are exactly the cells with C = 0, so F' = C' and F = C, which matches the 1s at m1, m3, m5, m7.

errata.claim: Q10 asks for the minimum DFA of F = Σm(0, 2, 4, 6).
errata.correction: The question asks for the minimal SOP, which is F = C'; no automaton is involved.

errata.claim: Q12: Σm(1, 3, 7) + d(0, 5) gives F = C or A' + BC, depending.
errata.correction: The unique minimum is F = C (m1, m3, m7 and don't-care m5). A' + BC is not even valid here, since it covers m2, which is 0.

errata.claim: PYQ-10: ABC + AB'C + ABC' + A'BC simplifies to AC + AB by consensus.
errata.correction: The function is Σm(3, 5, 6, 7), the majority AB + BC + CA. BC cannot be dropped because m3 = A'BC is covered only by BC.

errata.claim: PYQ-13: the minimal SOP of Σm(2, 4, 6, 8, 10) is BD' + AC'D'.
errata.correction: BD' covers the 0s m12 and m14. The minimal SOP is A'BD' + AB'D' + B'CD' (or A'CD' in place of B'CD'), with A'BD' and AB'D' essential.
